entry.title: What You're Actually Buying When You Pick an LLM Vendor
entry.summary: Reasoning benchmarks have converged, top 10 models sit within six GPQA points of each other, so the score on the comparison page barely differentiates vendors anymore. What still varies is refusal policy, cost-to-control ratio, and, for some providers, which country's content rules the model was built under. entry.title: An LLM judge is a biased instrument, not a measurement
entry.summary: Last month I shipped an eval that ranked two prompt variants. Variant A won by four points. A teammate reran the same eval the next morning and Variant B won. Same model, same judge, same test set. The only thing that changed was the order the two answers were pasted into the judge prompt. That is not a flake. entry.title: Test-Time Training for Modality Order Consistency in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: We find that vision-language models are sensitive to a specific semantically irrelevant change: the order in which the image and question are presented. Across three models and three benchmarks, image first prompting consistently outperforms question-first prompting, revealing a repeatable modality order failure.
